verdict.rationale: Jules' docs say it needs access to your repositories, clones the code into a VM, and creates a PR that you can approve, merge and publish on GitHub. Tasks can also be assigned through a "jules" label on GitHub issues. Community users independently describe good GitHub integration and usable PRs. missing for 10: detailed first-party documentation of the GitHub connection/authorization flow and repository permission scoping.

support.subject: As a developer, I can connect a GitHub repository so an agent can access the code and open pull requests against it

citations.quote: Jules needs access to your repositories in order to work.
Jules runs in a virtual machine where it clones your code, installs dependencies, and modifies files.
Jules creates a PR of the changes. Approve the PR, merge it to your branch, and publish it on GitHub.
Use the "jules" label in an issue to assign a task directly in GitHub.
